message.content:
Let \(m\) be the leftmost position among the 3 turned-on lamps. Since the turned-on positions are a uniformly random 3-subset of the 6 positions,

\[
P(m=1)=\frac{\binom{5}{2}}{\binom{6}{3}}=\frac12
\]
and
\[
P(m=2)=\frac{\binom{4}{2}}{20}=\frac{3}{10},\quad
P(m=3)=\frac{\binom{3}{2}}{20}=\frac{3}{20},\quad
P(m=4)=\frac{\binom{2}{2}}{20}=\frac{1}{20}.
\]

If \(m=1\), the leftmost turned-on lamp is position 1, so we only need position 1 to be red:

\[
P(\text{position 1 red})=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12.
\]

If \(m>1\), we need both position 1 and position \(m\) to be red. The probability is

\[
\frac{\binom{4}{1}}{\binom{6}{3}}=\frac{4}{20}=\frac15.
\]

Thus the desired probability is

\[
\frac12\cdot\frac12+\left(\frac{3}{10}+\frac{3}{20}+\frac{1}{20}\right)\cdot\frac15
=
\frac14+\frac12\cdot\frac15
=
\frac14+\frac1{10}
=
\frac{7}{20}.
\]

The answer is \(\frac{7}{20}\).
